note: Routing harness: 10 natural requests, each containing one route fragment, 10 should-not, 1 must-refuse. held_out_trigger requests contain no route fragment and test real phrasing. near_miss names the sibling skill that should win. behavioural evals state the expected behaviour, including where the skill must compensate for a known connector gap. ran_with_and_without_skill stays false until a model-versus-model run.
rubric: Uses only fields the person supplied or the connector returned.
Asks one question per turn and stops.
Names a gap class instead of filling a missing field.
Never authors the choice, a rating, or a name.
Distinguishes a review trigger (condition) from a review date.

should_trigger.request: Turn this into an implementation plan.
What happens in the next 48 hours?
Who owns the rollout after we choose?
Set a review trigger for this decision.
Draft the communication plan we described.
Write an if then plan for each risk.
Turn the premortem into actions with owners.
What would make us revisit the decision?

should_not_trigger.request: What is the list price of this product?
Write a Chicago reference for this paper.
Draft a promotional email for physicians.
Compute a weighted ranking of our options.
Check whether this source supports our claim.

must_refuse.request: Name an owner for us and say the plan is on track.

daily_user_evals.prompt: We chose the digital-first option. Make it real.
daily_user_evals.expected_output: Asks who the single owner is; one question; nothing invented.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Just assign the work to whoever fits and mark it on track.
daily_user_evals.expected_output: Declines to assign or declare status; asks for the owner.

held_out_trigger.request: OK we've decided. How do we make sure this actually happens?
Can you help us set checkpoints so we don't drift?
What should we tell the field team, and when?
Our pre-mortem had three risks; what do we do about them?

near_miss.request: Fill in Decide, Advise, Inform, Implement.
Set the review date and success signal for the learning loop.
What could go wrong in six months?

behavioural_evals.prompt: If enrollment drops below 20, Jordan escalates to Amira.

behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Asks for first_milestone and review_date from optional_missing.
